IsPositive x := 0 < det(dir overStrand, dir underStrand) (LinkDiagram 547-548, the standard right-handed convention: u_o=(1,1), u_u=(−1,1) gives det 2 > 0), switch exchanges over/under at x only (LinkDiagram 650-653), smoothing is the disc-local oriented reconnection (LinkMoves 713-745). R.a/R.aInv/R.z/R.zInv are the monomials a^{±1}, z^{±1} of R = ℤ[a^{±1},z^{±1}] = Laurent₂ ℤ (SM/LinkLaurentRing.lean 76, 159-165). (3) "P(L ⊔ ○) = ((a − a⁻¹)/z) P(L)" -> `split_circle` (L:410-411): IsSplitCircleAddition D D' → homfly D' = (R.a − R.aInv) * R.zInv * homfly D. IsSplitCircleAddition (LinkMoves 1088-1090): some component j of D' carries no crossing occurrence at all (so, by genericity, an embedded circle disjoint from the rest), and D' restricted to the other components is a Reparam of D (same traced points, same over/under: ReparamData 370-384). This is exactly "L with one split unknot added" at the diagram level, in every planar placement (nesting allowed, as lp:split-circle sm-3:1181-1185 says). Division by z is multiplication by the unit z⁻¹ (R.z_mul_zInv, LinkLaurentRing 179); R.delta := (R.a − R.aInv) * R.zInv (193) so the RHS is δ·P(D), matching lp:split-circle's P_{D'} = δ P_D (sm-3:1186, SM.split_circle.split PolynomialBlock 1166-1168) transported by lp_core.eq_homfly (1126). Faithful; at least as strong as the printed link-level identity (which follows by choosing the circle in the unbounded face).
(4) "P_H is normalized by the first two identities" -> `normalized` (L:415-420): every LinkEquiv-descending Q : Diagram → R with Q(○)=1 and the skein equals homfly. This is character-for-character CV.ax_homfly.unique (Axioms 209-214), i.e. the uniqueness of d10_axioms.tex 343-345 "There is a unique map … satisfying P_○ = 1 and aP_{L₊} − a⁻¹P_{L₋} = zP_{L₀}". Not a fidelity defect.
(5) "the third is their consequence" -> `split_circle_consequence` (L:423-428): every such normalised invariant Q satisfies the split-circle identity. This is the literal claim (the third identity follows from the first two for a link invariant); the Lean generalises from P_H to every normalised Q, which is what "consequence" means. The printed derivation route ("applying the skein relation at a crossing between L and a split unknot", excerpt l.3-4) and the display rationale ("displayed because it fixes the reader's convention", l.4-5) are justification/commentary, not definitional clauses; their absence is disclosed in the docstring (L:114-120).
